project_goal: Mature the SPY-focused MVP into a reproducible volatility trading lab with versioned experiments, strategy registries, retraining, replay, execution simulation, reports, and merge/stop governance.

comparison.after: Baseline work is documented as a versioned candidate for review.
comparison.before: Several uncommitted MVP upgrades mixed with generated artifacts.

comparison.after: Auxiliary files are ignored while source slides and final PDF remain trackable.
comparison.before: LaTeX auxiliary files appeared as untracked review noise.

versions.goal: Freeze the current dirty MVP state without reverting existing work, separate source artifacts from build junk, and produce a baseline report.
versions.main_outcome: Current execution layer, walk-forward retraining, neural BSDE replay, README narrative, and presentation assets are treated as the baseline candidate.
versions.merge_evidence: Current status, smoke results, and known risks.
risks: Baseline includes prior uncommitted Execution Layer and walk-forward changes that still need final merge review.
Some smoke gates depend on local SPY data under demo/data, which is intentionally gitignored.

comparison.after: Repo-local version reports and machine-readable version metadata.
comparison.before: Ad hoc README updates and chat summaries.

comparison.after: Single smoke-gate CLI with required core gates and optional model gates.
Datasets, strategies, and gates are declared in registries.
comparison.before: Signals and datasets are discoverable only by reading code and README.

versions.goal: Add the lab control plane: registries, smoke gates, version reports, and explicit merge/hold/stop recommendations.
versions.main_outcome: Every future upgrade can be recorded, smoke-tested, reported, and reviewed before merge.
versions.merge_evidence: Required smoke gates pass and generated report includes a recommendation.
risks: Model gates remain optional because ONNX Runtime and training dependencies are machine-local.
The lab registry is intentionally descriptive in v0.1; it does not yet drive C++ strategy construction.

comparison.after: SPY panel and legacy ATM fallback have explicit registry entries and schema files.
comparison.before: SPY data assumptions lived in README prose and C++/Python call sites.

comparison.after: A data contract gate checks columns, timestamps, numeric fields, quote bounds, date summaries, and walk-forward causality before replay.
comparison.before: Replay failures were the first signal that local data was missing or malformed.

comparison.after: Validation emits machine-readable JSON and a Markdown report that can be attached to each lab version.
comparison.before: Dataset summaries were ad hoc terminal observations.

versions.goal: Formalize SPY panel schema, data quality checks, dataset catalog, and date/window summaries.
versions.merge_evidence: Schema and quality gates pass on the local SPY panel.
risks: The validator checks local structural quality, not vendor provenance or corporate-action adjustments.
The legacy ATM fallback remains intentionally limited and should not be used for full strategy research.

comparison.after: Strategies and signal components are validated against a strategy schema.
comparison.before: Strategy registry entries were descriptive but not mechanically checked.

comparison.after: A Markdown catalog is generated from the registry with family, hedger, status, edge, replay command, inputs, and risks.
comparison.before: The strategy library existed across README prose and C++ headers.

comparison.after: The smoke gate now requires strategy registry validation before build/replay.
comparison.before: New techniques could be added without satisfying minimum metadata or replay-command standards.

versions.goal: Turn current signals into a registered volatility strategy library.
versions.merge_evidence: Strategy registry and replay comparison report.
risks: Registered signal components are not automatically tradable until wired into alpha_runner or research gates.
Replay commands are shape-validated in v0.3; future versions should execute per-strategy replay plans.

comparison.after: A single experiment CLI produces manifest.json, summary.json, summary.md, logs, and replay CSVs under one experiment directory.
comparison.before: Replay, model smoke, registry validation, and reports were separate commands.

comparison.after: The smoke gate now requires the experiment orchestrator to validate registries, build alpha_runner, replay BS delta, and write experiment summaries.
comparison.before: The lab gates verified pieces but did not prove a user-facing experiment pipeline existed.

comparison.after: Model profile experiments can include ONNX neural replay and walk-forward smoke when local dependencies are available.
comparison.before: Model replay and walk-forward smoke were available only as individual gate steps.

versions.goal: Unify alpha replay, walk-forward retraining, plotting, and report generation.
versions.merge_evidence: Experiment summary and gated replay outputs.
risks: The orchestrator smoke focuses on compact replay and report generation; full plotting remains tied to alpha_pnl_test_runner outputs.
v0.4 runs per-experiment validations and builds, so the gate is intentionally redundant but more user-facing.

comparison.after: Rough-vol research gates and candidate ideas are declared in a research registry with schema-backed validation.
comparison.before: Research evidence lived in README prose and scattered output folders.

comparison.after: The lab gate runner and experiment orchestrator now validate research-gate evidence before replay.
comparison.before: Data and strategy registries were gated, but research claims were not.

comparison.after: New candidates for calendar term structure, vol-of-vol regime filtering, and event-risk filtering are recorded with decision rules.
comparison.before: Future research ideas were implicit and not tied to promotion/rejection criteria.

versions.goal: Add new candidate volatility techniques under the same gates.
versions.merge_evidence: New strategy hypotheses are falsified or promoted through registry-first gates.
risks: v0.5 validates existing research evidence and candidate readiness; it does not rerun heavy historical sweeps.
Candidate ideas need expanded data contracts before they can become tradable strategies.
